event: Vukradin played the Moonlight Sonata for the grieving mother drake; it did not argue with grief but sat with the difficulty.
quote: I raised my instrument. I want to be precise about this: I did not play something cheerful. I did not play something that tried to explain or fix or reframe. A grieving mother does not need to be persuaded that things will be alright. She knows they won't. The young is dead. That is the situation and it will remain the situation. What I played instead was something that simply... named the shape of it. The Moonlight Sonata has a patience to it — it does not rush toward resolution, it sits with the difficulty of a thing and lets the phrases fall like stones settling into water. It does not argue with grief. It says: yes, this is heavy, here, I'll hold the other end.
